items.author: Newsroom
items.excerpt: One woman died and another was hospitalized with suspected food poisoning after eating eggs cooked with stinging nettles in the Tarsus district of Türkiye's southern Mersin province on Wednesday, T24 reported. Durdane Ogmac, 55, and her cousin Nuran Ogmac, 53, prepared the dish during an olive harvest in the Beylice neighborhood but fell ill shortly after eating it. Stinging nettle is an edible herb that is typically cooked before consumption to neutralize its stinging hairs. Emergency medical personnel and gendarmerie officers were dispatched to the scene after relatives alerted authorities.
